title: Craft Blend 2-Mix Solo #08 (MoroccanZellige+RomanianHorezu)
prompt:
Image format: a vertical portrait-orientation photograph, 2:3 aspect ratio, taller than it is wide.

A full-body photograph with a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult Indian woman in her early 40s, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, kohl-lined almond eyes, a small gold bindi, a deep maroon-red lip, warm golden-brown skin, cheerful, cool ash-grey hair styled in a crown braid wrapping around the head, real living eyes. Long almond nails, glittery finish.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person. A dramatically impossible waist-to-hip ratio dominates her silhouette: a colossal heavy bust, an extremely sharply cinched waist pulled in far tighter than the waistline of any of her other curves, and then enormous round hips flaring out to a width many times greater than that narrow waist. Gigantic soft thighs pressed together, very thick soft arms, a gigantic rounded rear. Her head looks small on top of her massive body. Not a plus-size model, not evenly proportioned. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, a smooth taut surface with natural creases and shadow only where the flesh folds. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted in two different patterns covering every inch of her body below the jaw with no bare skin anywhere. Her LEFT side is painted in Moroccan zellige tile mosaic (a deep cobalt ground with interlocking white, terracotta and gold motifs), wide gold bands following every deep crease, dense interlocking star-and-cross motifs filling the space between bands, pigment on living skin. Her RIGHT side is painted in Romanian Horezu ceramic (a cream ground with green, brown and ochre spiral floral motifs), wide ochre bands following every crease, dense spiral floral bands filling the space between bands, pigment on living skin. Rather than a sharp boundary, the two painted patterns blend gradually into each other across a soft irregular zone a few inches wide, motifs from each pattern scattered into the other's territory, density fading rather than stopping abruptly, face unpainted.

Pose: square to camera, feet wide, arms clear of her body.

Footwear: extreme platform stiletto Mary Janes, painted with the blended patterns following the same soft transitions as her skin.

Background & Lighting: the blended painted patterns reading crisp against her skin, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Vertical 2:3 portrait-orientation full-body photograph, taller than it is wide. portrait 2:3 vertical.
